clue.text: Yellow butter, on the turn, gone off in dish

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, and so does chicken

indicators.note: something on the turn is turning round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a ram

indicators.note: gone off suggests spoilt or disordered, so these four letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Yellowing butter that has turned rancid is found in some dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' turns RAM into MAR; 'off' jumbles GONE into ENGO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic French chicken dish named after Napoleon's battle, so it is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Stars in endless musical roles — no time to entertain surrealist

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Camelot is a stage musical

indicators.note: to entertain means to hold inside as a guest
no time means the letter T for time is taken out

parts.note: roles in a play are parts
Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter

explanation.surface: Stars of an unending musical's roles lack time for a surrealist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last T and 'no time' removes another T; 'to entertain' wraps the shortened roles word, PARS, round the painter. Camelot is a stage musical about King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelopardalis is the giraffe constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Spoil most of river and lake with emptied garbage

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Indus is a river in South Asia

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving the first and last

explanation.surface: Garbage and a lake ruin a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge a child is to spoil it by giving it whatever it wants.

clue.text: Rogue English King, securing the front, goes northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue going northwards means reading upwards
securing means holding inside

parts.note: the van is the front of an army

explanation.surface: A rogue English monarch, having taken the front line, retreats north.
explanation.walkthrough: E and K hold VAN, making EVANK, and 'goes northwards' turns it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a rogue.

clue.text: One breaking fruitcake split for food

parts.note: a fruitcake is a crazy person, a nut

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into the middle of

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a fruitcake in two to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a nourishing substance, so it means food.

clue.text: Move nothing at all to turn up demons

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: to stir is to move
FA is short for Fanny Adams, slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Doing nothing at all is enough to bring up some demons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses STIRFA. Sweet Fanny Adams is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrits are powerful demons from Arabian folklore.

clue.text: Queen wearing way out crown one makes shift to destroy

indicators.note: makes shift means this letter is moved to another place
wearing means having this letter attached

parts.note: an exit is a way out
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen
the pate is the crown of the head
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A queen in a crown finds a makeshift way out to wreck things.
explanation.walkthrough: EXIT, R and PATE make EXITRPATE; 'makes shift' moves the I one place along, giving EXTIRPATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out completely, to destroy.

clue.text: Damn taps behave inconsistently

parts.note: blow is a mild oath, like damn
the two taps on a basin are hot and cold

explanation.surface: Someone curses the plumbing for being erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for keep changing one's mind.

clue.text: Count inviting Duke on a horse for host of party

indicators.note: inviting means taking in as a guest, so this word goes inside the other

parts.note: to count is to matter, as in 'it doesn't count'
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A nobleman asks a duke riding a horse to come to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER takes in D, H and A, giving MA-DHA-TTER; the A follows the horse's H rather than sitting where the clue order puts it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's Alice, this character hosts the famous mad tea party.

clue.text: Catch sharp tool on sides of timber

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other part
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an awl is a sharp pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A woodworker grabs a pointed tool resting on the edges of a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to fish with a dragged net, so it means to catch fish.

clue.text: City left with English housing problem

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so these letters go round the next part

parts.note: ill as a noun means a trouble or problem

explanation.surface: Someone has left town with an English housing problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France.

clue.text: Bury opinion in an examination

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a view is an opinion

explanation.surface: Someone buries their real opinion during a formal exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A job interview is a formal questioning, a kind of examination of a candidate.

clue.text: Nice excuses offered by worker

parts.note: pleas are excuses offered in defence
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee offers nice excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are everyday synonyms meaning agreeable.

clue.text: Police officer not in hiding volunteers to be witness

indicators.note: hiding means holding concealed inside
not means the following word is removed

parts.note: an inspector is a police officer
this word is the letters taken out
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A police officer, not hiding, sees volunteers testify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' strips two letters from the police officer, leaving SPECTOR, and 'hiding' wraps that round the volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, someone who witnesses an event.

clue.text: Stare at lad failing to finish outhouse

parts.note: to gaze is to stare

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a boy who cannot complete his task in the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small garden building, a kind of summerhouse or outhouse.

clue.text: Could it hide one who is prone to lying?

definitions.text: Could it hide one who is prone to lying?

parts.words: Could it hide one who is prone to lying?
parts.note: prone to lying suggests a liar, but here means someone lying down in bed under a cover

explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a bedspread, which covers a person lying in bed.

clue.text: Steer with this runs in front of a little cow

indicators.note: in front of means this letter comes before the next part

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an udder is a small part of a cow

explanation.surface: A steering instruction about running ahead of a small calf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little cow' means a part of a cow, its udder, not a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the blade by which a boat is steered.

clue.text: See document with directions I must enter

indicators.note: must enter means going inside

parts.note: doc is short for document
E, S and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: Look at a document whose directions must be followed.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area, also called a diocese.

clue.text: Animals noted gambolling in fresh air

indicators.note: in means one jumbled group sits inside the other
fresh suggests a new arrangement, so these letters are mixed up
gambolling means leaping about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Animals are seen frolicking in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gambolling' and 'fresh' each scramble their own word; 'in' then sets the jumbled noted (ODENT) inside the jumbled air (RIA).
explanation.definitionFit: Rodentia is the zoological order of rodents, a group of animals.

clue.text: Sums up time with friends

parts.note: allies are friends

explanation.surface: Someone sums up the time spent with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies as a verb means adds up, counts.

clue.text: Theologian in Tel Aviv ultimately feeding the first born?

indicators.note: feeding means going into the mouth of

parts.note: Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A theologian in Israel feeds a firstborn child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives L and V, which go into CAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: John Calvin was the French Protestant theologian of the Reformation.

clue.text: Numbers on a clock are in order

definitions.text: Numbers on a clock are in order

parts.words: Numbers on a clock are in order
parts.note: the figures on a clock sit round its dial, and a military command to turn round is an order

explanation.walkthrough: Clock numbers go round the face; read that way, the phrase is also the parade-ground command to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is the drill command to turn round, so it is an order given on parade.

clue.text: Get old cardinals without a sound

indicators.note: without here means outside, so these letters go round the A

parts.note: V, L, I and D are Roman numerals, the old way of writing cardinal numbers

explanation.surface: Gaining aged churchmen without making any noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' looks like churchmen, but cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, written the old way in Roman numerals. 'Get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is a valid one: both mean well founded.

clue.text: See cash almost raised in essential part of The Sting

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: money is cash

explanation.surface: Look at money almost raised for an essential part of the film The Sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MONEY to MONE and 'raised' turns it to ENOM. The Sting, a film, misleads; it is a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the poison that makes an insect's sting work.

clue.text: That is a fish, by the way

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone points out a fish, mentioning it in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase meaning that is, shortened to i.e.

clue.text: Film star, fast consumed by wine, pinching Clara's bottom

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the wine
pinching means grabbing and holding inside

parts.note: vino is an informal word for wine

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A screen idol, drunk on wine, gropes a woman named Clara.
explanation.walkthrough: VINO takes in A (the last letter of Clara) and LENT: V-ALENT-INO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was a famous silent film star.

clue.text: Royal statement forged a tremendous awe

indicators.note: forged means made up or shaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forged royal statement inspires great awe.
explanation.definitionFit: This remark is famously credited to Queen Victoria, using the royal we.
